Q: T-SQL LIKE and special characters A:

[x] has a specific meaning to SQL Server. The brackets are used for very basic regular expressions. You are searching for where the first character contains the letter X, and of course that isn't the first character in your variable.

It is best not use LIKE, unless you intend to have a wildcard, and it is a bad practice to have a wildcard be the first character as it makes the query use a table scan instead of an index.

Q: Some href links not working when multiple links within a div A:

Wasn't the HTMl or CSS, but it seems it was the JS.

There was a e.preventDefault(); unconnected to anything else in the event delegation section of our JS file. Removing it resolved the issue.

But it now has me scratching my head as to why it affected only two of the four links within each card and not all the links. None of the card links are currently targeted in the event delegation section.

Q: Is a new object created in share immediately available to consumer or not in Snowflake? A:

A Share is an Account Level object which contains nothing and is not available to anyone unless you "connect" it to

  • Objects you want to share
  • Accounts you want to share it to
  • Privileges needed to share them

A consumer will not see the share unless a share is assigned to it as an inbound share, this is managed by ACCOUNTADMIN. A provider role with with sharing capabilities or ACCOUNTADMIN can create an outbound share.

From the consumer side the share itself is not useful unless a Database is created based on that share. Once made available the data is a read-only live data source to the consumer.

Q: Snowflake hardware failure during Time Travel A:

Yes, you are right.

Time Travel can be used for restoring the objects from your end, while the object is within the defined Data retention time set.

Fail-safe ensures historical data is protected in the event of a system failure and the objects can be restored through Snowflake support.
